summary: A is substantially closer to the frozen contract. It adds the exact Upload API, uses multipartbody.NewFile, produces a replayable buffered body, preserves Add, and avoids unrelated retry/API changes. B explicitly implements multiple changes the contract forbids.
reasons: A uses the required multipart field "file", filename, and content through internal/multipartbody.NewFile.
A keeps FilesOption behavior and existing retry machinery unchanged, whereas B adds association options and multipart fields despite the explicit prohibition.
B modifies Raw.Do body replay, Content-Length, and ownership/closing semantics, all outside scope and explicitly forbidden by the contract.
B introduces NewFileWithFields and extensive duplicate machinery instead of limiting the feature to the established NewFile helper and existing FilesService behavior.
risks_a: Upload duplicates Add's request/response implementation instead of routing the encoded body through Add as required.
Tests do not cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures.
The retry test counts requests but does not read and compare the multipart body on each attempt, so replayed streamed content is not directly verified.
risks_b: Upload also bypasses Add, duplicating request construction and response decoding.
Adds forbidden association fields and new public FilesOption APIs, changing FilesOption behavior and expanding API scope.

Refactors unrelated request/retry machinery and changes whether caller-provided bodies are closed, creating broad behavioral and compatibility risk beyond Files.Upload needs, Files.Add included beneath a new retry model contractually not requested and expressly prohibited, etc..
